description: The figure consists of two vertically stacked bar charts illustrating the "% point difference" across a sequence of categories. In both charts, the horizontal axis serves as the category axis, displaying labels ordered sequentially from 0 to 12, followed by a final category named "concat". The bottom chart's horizontal axis is explicitly labeled "layer", and the text "XLM-R" is positioned between the two panels. The vertical axis in both charts represents the value, labeled "% point difference", utilizing a linear scale with a visible range from -10 to 0, marked by numeric tick labels and horizontal grid lines at intervals of 2. The top chart displays light blue bars with black outlines, showing predominantly negative values that generally increase (become less negative) from left to right. The most negative value in the top chart occurs at category 0 (approximately -10.5), while categories 9, 10, and "concat" show small positive values, with "concat" reaching the highest positive value of approximately 0.4. The bottom chart features darker blue bars with black outlines, exhibiting a similar increasing trend across the categories. Its most negative values are at categories 0 and 1 (both approximately -9.5), and it reaches small positive values at categories 10, 11, and "concat" (up to approximately 0.4). In both panels, the bars are arranged by the predefined sequence of the horizontal axis labels rather than being sorted by magnitude, and there are no grouped or stacked components.
